contentHtml:
In terms of travel, we are going to take you to the best train journeys in Europe. All you need to do is to sit back calmly, relax and enjoy the ride. Trains are one of the most popular means of transport for Europeans, so travellers can see everything in the comfort of their cabin at very reasonable prices. From romantic valleys to medieval castles, getting on a European train is one of the best ways to explore the country. Thanks to the great engineers of the Old Continent. Europe has an excellent train network that connects every point of the continent, from large metropolitan cities to remote, picturesque mountain villages.

El Transcantábrico, Spain

What’s better than experiencing the stunning natural beauty of northern Spain with a 5-star train? During this trip, you will stay in the original Pullman coaches from 1923.

The tour includes visiting the historic cities of the region, visiting the best beaches along the Bay of Biscay and boarding the train overnight. The journey begins in Irun, near the French border, and in eight days passes through San Sebastian, Asturias, Bilbao, Ferrol and Santander allowing passengers to see the best offers of northern Spain.

The Flam Railway, NorwayMyrdal to Flam

Considered one of Norway’s most famous tourist attractions, the Flam Railway should not be missed by travellers around the country. You can find cheap air tickets to Norway, especially between May to August which also is the best time to have this journey.

The trip by this railway leaves tourists staring at the views of mystical rivers and waterfalls, steep snowy mountain peaks and charming farms attached to the mountainside. At the bottom of the mountain, you can admire the picturesque landscapes of the Flam Valley and the beautiful Aurlandsfjord – the longest fjord in the world.

Caledonian Sleeper, The UK

The legendary Caledonian Sleeper has recently undergone a £150 million renovation, which seems to help restore the splendour of Britain’s most iconic night train. Caledonia Sleeper runs between London and Edinburgh and offers some of the most beautiful sunset views Scotland has to offer.

Classic rooms and even cabins look very elegant and the food served on the train is delicious. Overall, this is one train ride you can’t miss if you want to experience one of the best scenic train trips in Europe. If you get your flights to London to visit, do not miss this train journey. This will add to an unforgettable memory of your trip to the UK.

The Little Yellow Train, France

The little yellow train has been one of the most popular train journeys in France for over 100 years. The train journey begins in Villefranche-de-Conflent, leads through the Regional Natural Park of the Catalan Pyrenees, to the highest train station in France, Bolquere (1593 m), and ends at Latour-de-Carol-Enveitg.

And if you think it can’t be better then you are wrong; in summer the train rides with an open wagon. Another good thing about this trip is that you don’t have to worry about booking tickets in advance or not being able to find a ticket if you book in advance. Tickets for the small yellow train can only be bought at the train station before travelling.

The Golden Pass, Switzerland, Lucerne to Montreux

If you want to taste everything that Switzerland has to offer, the Golden Pass is a train journey. This lovely tour includes panoramic cars that allow you to watch 360 degrees for almost the entire train journey and VIP seat options if you’re looking for a first-class experience.

Along with houses covered with flowers, the Brünig Pass, vineyards, lakes and one of the most historic cities in the country, the Golden Pass is a piece of heaven hidden in the Swiss countryside. We all know that Switzerland is by far the most beautiful place on the face of the earth. Try to get cheap air tickets to Switzerland so that you may have much more to spend on this train journey.

Rhine Valley Line, Germany, Mainz to Koblenz

Of all the train journeys in Germany, the central railway on the Rhine is one of the best train journeys in Europe, epitomizing the quintessential German landscape. This picturesque route, filled with terraced slopes and 14th-century castles, chases some of the quaintest wine countries in Europe. Stopping in every village along the way, you won’t miss Mark's burg castles.

Kalavryta Railway, Greece

Greece may be far more known for its divine white-sand beaches, but a list of the best scenic trains in Europe would not be complete without Kalawrita. This is one of the last remaining gauge lines on the Peloponnese (most were cut off due to the financial crisis in Greece).

The railway line connects the two mountain towns of Diakopto and Kalavryta, passing near the historic site of Olympia and the seemingly endless stretch of beautiful, wild scenery that will make you feel like in Switzerland, not in Greece.

Paris to Moscow

Every Thursday, the Russian Railways train begins an epic journey from Paris Central Station, usually arriving in Moscow on Saturday morning. The train passes through France, Germany, Poland and Belarus before entering Russia.

When travelling, you can expect the best of Europe in 2 days as the train passes through its heart. This is certainly one of the most classic ways to move between two continents. And if this doesn’t seem exhaustive, check out the last trip on this list.

Conclusion:

Get your cheap air tickets to Europe to enjoy any of these train journeys, you won’t regret a second, that is our promise. To save one or two dollars, consider investing in a rail pass. The ticket is valid for thousands of places throughout Europe and helps to travel by train at a lower price.
